title: Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Medical Image Segmentation Using Latent Transform Networks
abstract: Proposes PPCMI-SF combining skip-connected image/mask autoencoders, client-specific orthogonal Keyed Latent Transforms (KLT via QR decomposition), and a server-side overcomplete Unified Mapping Network (UMN with Pyramid Pooling).
source_excerpt: On Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation (5,635 images), PPCMI-SF achieved 76.90% DSC, 11.23 HD95, and 4.25 ASD (improving over Privacy-SF baseline at 69.45% DSC, 13.13 HD95, 5.79 ASD, and approaching non-private UNet 80.32% and FATNet 80.55%). Cross-decoder inversion SSIM dropped from 0.69 to 0.34, MIA AUC=0.473 (random guessing), with 19.07 ms/query latency (0.88 MB payload).

title: Physics Driven Domain Specific Transporter Framework with Attention Mechanism for Ultrasound Imaging
abstract: Unsupervised keypoint discovery on 171 3D Wrist Ultrasound sweeps (113 train, 58 test, 256 frames/sweep, Philips iU22 13-MHz) integrating Distance-Gain Attenuation, directional Radon/Inverse-Radon filtering, monogenic local phase + feature symmetry + integrated backscatter (RT-FPM), and CBAM-augmented KeyNet.
source_excerpt: On 58 test 3D wrist ultrasound videos, the physics-driven Transporter with CBAM attention and frame-averaging achieved Specificity=0.72 and Sensitivity=0.74 (vs vanilla Transporter SP=0.47, SN=0.69), unsupervisedly tracking distal radial metaphysis, epiphysis, and carpal bone fracture discontinuities.

title: Wrist bone segmentation in X-ray images using CT-based simulations
authors: A ElTantawy, A Karantana, X Chen
abstract: Generates 9,240 simulated DRR X-rays from 88 wrist CT volumes (18 subjects) across -70° to +70° projection angles using Beer-Lambert attenuation, 99th-percentile metal clipping, and soft-tissue percentile reduction to train nnU-Net for 10-bone wrist segmentation.
source_excerpt: Evaluated on 912 simulated test radiographs (4 subjects, 19 CTs) and 121 real clinical radiographs, nnU-Net achieved mean Dice of 0.92 at 0°-20° (AP view), 0.89 at 40°, and 0.80 at 70° (lateral view). Per-bone AP Dice: Radius 0.95, Lunate 0.94, Hamate 0.94, Trapezium 0.94, Pisiform 0.93, Ulna 0.92, Scaphoid 0.92, Capitate 0.92 (0.67 at 70°), Triquetrum 0.86, Trapezoid 0.84.

title: Unconstrained Kinematic MRI Tracking of Wrist Carpal Bones
abstract: Tracks 3D kinematics of scaphoid, lunate, and capitate during unconstrained ulnar-radial deviation and flexion-extension on 5 subjects using 3T dynamic LAVA Flex water-reconstructed MRI (12 slices, 2.57s/frame) and 6-DoF point-cloud ICP registration.
source_excerpt: Achieved 88%-95% carpal bone surface coverage with total rotation error of 1.9°±1.8° (ulnar-radial) and 3.0°±4.6° (flexion-extension) and COM translation error of 0.30±0.47 mm (UR) and 0.72±0.80 mm (FE) at 2.57s/frame, successfully detecting an occult structural capitate abnormality in Subject 1.

title: Development and Stability Analysis of Carpal Kinematic Metrics from 4D Magnetic Resonance Imaging
authors: A Sharafi, AS Nencka, KM Koch
abstract: Automates 4D MRI carpal kinematic profiling across 49 subjects (29 asymptomatic controls, 20 symptomatic prior wrist injury) using MONAI SegResNet 3D segmentation, Radius-based ISB coordinate registration, modified z-score outlier filtering, and 1st/2nd-order polynomial regression of scaphoid/lunate vs capitate (120 metrics).
source_excerpt: Identified 17 kinematic metrics with high intra-subject repeatability (ICC(3)>0.7: 10 in radial-ulnar, 7 in flexion-extension), 16 of which also showed high inter-subject stability (ICC(1)>0.7) in controls. Asymptomatic subjects had 25 stable metrics (ICC>0.7) vs only 12 in symptomatic injured wrists (90th percentile ICC 0.76 vs 0.68), with quadratic curvature coefficients showing the largest stability loss in injured wrists.

title: How many radiographs are needed to re-train a deep learning system for object detection?
abstract: Systematically benchmarks YOLOv5s retraining sample complexity across 16 dataset sizes (16 to 256 radiographs from 396 annotated DMPLO carpal radiographs) for 6 carpal classes including the vestigial first carpal bone (0.1% of image area).
source_excerpt: Training with >=96 radiographs (48 positive, 48 negative) achieved Precision, Recall, and mAP@0.5 > 0.95 across all carpal classes. At n=240 radiographs, YOLOv5s reached overall Precision=0.985, Recall=0.996, and mAP@0.5=0.990 (First carpal bone: Precision=0.925, Recall=1.000, mAP@0.5=0.972).

title: Attention-Guided Discriminative Region Localization and Label Distribution Learning for Bone Age Assessment
abstract: Proposes weakly-supervised attention-guided region localization (Hand H, Region-1 Carpal Bones R1, Region-2 Metacarpals R2 via erasing E) and Joint Age Distribution Learning + Expectation Regression (KL divergence + L1 MAE loss) on ~12,600 RSNA hand/wrist radiographs.
source_excerpt: Phase 1 localized Carpal Bones (R1) as the single most discriminative region (mIoU=0.722, AP50=0.965), reducing MAE from 7.3 months (full image L1) to 6.1 months (L1) and 5.3 months (LDL+ER), outperforming Full Hand (5.6 mo) and Metacarpals (6.2 mo). Multi-region ensemble (H+R1+R2 or H+R1+E) with LDL achieved 4.3 months MAE without any bounding-box or keypoint annotations.
